name: India
cultural_context_notes: Rich oral tradition, regional diversity (Panchatantra, Jataka tales, Baital Pachisi, Yakshas, Daayans, modern haunted sites and paranormal rumours).

name: United States
cultural_context_notes: Colonial folklore, regional tall tales, distinct Indigenous oral traditions (handled with distinct tribal attribution), modern cryptids (Mothman, Jersey Devil), and classic urban legends.

name: Japan
cultural_context_notes: Extensive yōkai, yūrei, and kaidan traditions; modern school ghost stories (gakkō no kaidan), Kuchisake-onna, Teke Teke, and cursed media urban legends.

name: Mexico
cultural_context_notes: Syncretic pre-Hispanic (Nahua, Maya) and colonial traditions, La Llorona, El Chupacabra, La Planchada, and contemporary urban legends.

name: Ireland
cultural_context_notes: Gaelic mythology, Tuatha Dé Danann, Aos Sí (fairies), banshees, National Folklore Collection archives, and modern haunted roads and phantom hitchhikers.

name: United Kingdom
cultural_context_notes: English, Scottish, and Welsh regional folklore, Arthurian legends, Black Shuck, phantom coaches, Spring-heeled Jack, and modern haunted tube stations.

name: Brazil
cultural_context_notes: Indigenous Tupi-Guarani, African diaspora, and Portuguese folklore syncretism; Saci-Pererê, Curupira, Boto Cor-de-Rosa, Loira do Banheiro.

name: Greece
cultural_context_notes: Ancient mythic continuity, Kallikantzaroi (winter goblins), Vrykolakas (revenants), Nereids, and modern Athens metro and highway urban legends.

name: China
cultural_context_notes: Classical Zhiguai and Chuanqi tales (Pu Songling's Liaozhai), fox spirits (Huli Jing), hungry ghosts, and modern urban legends such as Beijing Bus 375.

name: Nigeria
cultural_context_notes: Yoruba, Igbo, Hausa, and Edo oral literature, trickster tales (Tortoise / Ijapa), Mami Wata, and contemporary urban legends (Madam Koi Koi, Bush Baby).

name: South Korea
cultural_context_notes: Dangun mythology, Dokkaebi (goblins), Gumiho (nine-tailed fox), Cheonyeo Gwishin (virgin ghost), and modern urban legends (fan death, subway elevators, red paper blue paper).

name: Philippines
cultural_context_notes: Lower mythological creatures (Aswang, Manananggal, Kapre, Tikbalang), regional epics (Biag ni Lam-ang), and modern urban legends (White Lady of Balete Drive).

name: Indonesia
cultural_context_notes: Javanese, Sundanese, Balinese animist and maritime traditions; Kuntilanak, Pocong, Genderuwo, Nyi Roro Kidul, and modern haunted railway crossings.

name: Egypt
cultural_context_notes: Ancient mythological retellings, Coptic folklore, Islamic-era folklore (Afrit, Jinn, El Nedaha / Siren of the Nile), and modern Cairo Baron Palace urban legends.

name: Germany
cultural_context_notes: Grimm fairy tales, regional Sage legends (Pied Piper of Hamelin, Lorelei, Rübezahl, Wolpertinger), and modern German highway / suburban urban legends.
